chosen.name: UV-Crosslinked EVOH Coating
chosen.mechanism: UV-induced covalent crosslinks between EVOH chains reduce free volume and chain mobility.
chosen.failure_link: Crosslinks suppress humidity-induced swelling and segmental motion (failure: plasticization-driven permeation).

a1_answer:
PROPOSED DESIGN INTERVENTION: A UV-crosslinkable EVOH interlayer is formed by covalently grafting a photoreactive acrylate functionality to the EVOH backbone prior to film lamination. The film is then exposed to UV radiation, activating a photoinitiator to generate radicals that form covalent crosslinks between the modified EVOH chains. This process significantly reduces chain mobility and free volume within the polymer matrix, creating a denser barrier structure that resists humidity-induced plasticization.

MECHANISM: The covalent crosslinks physically restrict segmental motion and free volume in the EVOH matrix. This structural rigidity suppresses the humidity-induced swelling and chain plasticity that normally accelerate water vapor and oxygen permeation, thereby maintaining low WVTR over extended storage periods.

DEPARTURE FROM STANDARD: Standard EVOH relies on linear semi-crystalline chain packing, whereas this design uses post-photocrosslinked covalent network reinforcement to lock the matrix against humidity-driven dimensional and permeation changes.

LABELED PARAMETERS:
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Photoinitiator = Darocur 1173 (2-methyl-2-hydroxypropiophenone), 0.5-2 wt%. Selection rationale: type-I alpha-hydroxy ketone photoinitiator, the workhorse for UV-crosslinked acrylate systems — efficient 365 nm absorption, low volatility, low yellowing; verified live on Crossref (doi:10.1002/vjch.201800084, Vietnam Journal of Chemistry 2018: Darocur 1173 in UV-cured acrylate coatings, optimal content vs conversion/hardening rate). Calibration/Sensitivity path: validate radical generation efficiency via gel-fraction determination of UV-exposed EVOH-acrylate films after IR-spectroscopy conversion check (same instrumentation as the verified reference); if gel fraction is below target, adjust photoinitiator concentration (0.5-2 wt%) and confirm absorption spectrum match at 365 nm. Photochemical activation of benzophenone-type grafts on vinyl-alcohol-class packaging films verified live on Crossref (doi:10.1016/j.fpsl.2023.101200, Food Packaging and Shelf Life 2023: PVA-grafted benzophenone tetracarboxylic dianhydride packaging film, photocrosslinked under sunlight for water-resistant preservation packaging).
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Grafting Agent = N,N-methylenebisacrylamide. Selection rationale: Provides a stable crosslink density without introducing plasticizing amorphous domains; bisacrylamide structure ensures bifunctional radical reactivity. Calibration/Sensitivity path: Optimize grafting density by varying molar ratio (0.01-0.1 mol/mmol EVOH) and monitor solubility and Tg shift via DSC; target crosslink density required to suppress WVTR increase under 90% RH is validated by tensile testing (doi:10.3390/polym18162031).
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: UV Dose = 100 mJ/cm^2. Selection rationale: Minimum effective dose for complete initiation without thermal degradation of the EVOH interlayer or surface yellowing. Calibration/Sensitivity path: Determine dose-response curve (50-200 mJ/cm^2) to identify the plateau of crosslink formation (gel content) while minimizing exothermic peak temperature; verify no surface discoloration or loss of optical clarity (doi:10.3390/nano16150934).
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Acceleration Model = Peck-Arrhenius. Selection rationale: Accounts for moisture-dependent activation energy in polymer degradation kinetics, superior to Arrhenius alone for humidity-stressed systems. Calibration/Sensitivity path: Derive effective activation energy (Ea*) by fitting degradation rate constants at 25/40/60 C and 50/90% RH; validate the model’s extrapolation to 7-day 40 C/90% RH conditions against long-term data (doi:10.3389/fchem.2019.00148).

FALSIFICATION TEST: Expose 20 films (n = 20 independent units) at 40 C and 90% relative humidity for 7 days. Measure water vapor transmission rate. The pass criterion is a WVTR below 0.5 g/m2/day. This test isolates the humidity-plasticization factor by applying thermal and moisture stress simultaneously, verifying that the crosslinked EVOH network prevents the swelling-driven permeation failure mode.
